newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge union expects money offer today.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge union expects money offer today.

text.p: The union representing Falconbridge Ltd's Sudbury, Ontario workers said on Tuesday it expected to receive a monetary offer from the company later today.
Canadian Auto Workers union spokesman Rolly Gauthier also said the union and the company agreed to a news blackout.
"We expect the money package to come down some time today. As of noon there will be a news blackout until Friday," Gauthier said in a telephone interview.
The current contract expires at 0800 EDT/1200 GMT on Friday, August 1. Gauthier said workers would strike if there was no agreement by then.
"There is either a deal or we're out," he said.
Earlier this month, Falconbridge's 1,400 unionized mine workers in Sudbury voted 91.28 percent in favor of giving their negotiating team a strike mandate.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations produced 42,100 tonnes of nickel, 48,800 tonnes of copper and 730 tonnes of cobalt last year.
